answers.question: What is the scavenge air pressure at full load?
answers.expected_fact: 2.4 bar
answers.answer: According to document [1], "Scavenge air pressure at full load is 2.4 bar."

answers.question: At what lubricating oil pressure does the main engine shut down automatically?
answers.expected_fact: 2.2 bar
answers.answer: According to document [1], the automatic shutdown of the main engine occurs at 2.2 bar.

answers.question: What is the auxiliary boiler working pressure?
answers.expected_fact: 7 bar

answers.question: What jacket cooling water outlet temperature is maintained at the main engine?
answers.expected_fact: eighty-five degrees Celsius
answers.answer: The jacket cooling water outlet temperature from the main engine is maintained at eighty-five degrees Celsius. [1]

answers.question: How long is the bunker sample retained on board after delivery?
answers.expected_fact: twelve months
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, the bunker delivery note is retained for three years. However, the bunker sample itself is retained on board for twelve months.

answers.question: Within how long must the emergency generator connect to the emergency switchboard after a blackout?
answers.expected_fact: forty-five seconds
answers.answer: According to document index "1" title="Machinery Space Emergency Procedures", the emergency generator starts automatically and connects to the emergency switchboard within forty-five seconds after a loss of main electrical power.

answers.question: What temperature does the fuel oil purifier run at, and how many running hours between overhauls?
answers.expected_fact: ninety-eight degrees Celsius, overhauled every 2000 running hours
answers.answer: According to document [1], the fuel oil purifier operates at ninety-eight degrees Celsius. The interval for overhaul is every 2000 running hours.

answers.question: What is the chloride limit for boiler water and what is it for the closed jacket cooling circuit?
answers.expected_fact: boiler water 100 ppm, jacket cooling water 50 ppm
answers.answer: The provided documents state that the chloride limit for boiler water must not exceed 100 parts per million. In contrast, the chloride limit for the closed jacket cooling circuit is lower, at 50 parts per million.

answers.question: Which is kept on board longer, the Oil Record Book or the Ballast Water Record Book?
answers.expected_fact: Oil Record Book three years; Ballast Water Record Book two years on board
answers.answer:
The provided documents state that the Ballast Water Record Book is retained on board for two years from the date of the last entry, and thereafter under the company's control for a further three years. In contrast, the Oil Record Book is retained on board for only three years from the date of the last entry.

Therefore, the Ballast Water Record Book is kept on board longer than the Oil Record Book. [1]

answers.question: How often is the emergency generator tested and what must it achieve when it starts?
answers.expected_fact: run on load monthly; must connect within forty-five seconds
answers.answer:
According to document [1], the emergency generator is run on load monthly. 

The automatic start on loss of main power is tested at the same interval as the monthly test, but the specific requirement that it reach the switchboard within a defined time is stated in the emergency instruction.

answers.question: If we keep the ship going very slowly for a long time, how low can the power be set before it stops being allowed?
answers.expected_fact: fifteen per cent of maximum continuous rating
answers.answer: According to document "Machinery Space Emergency Procedures" [2], when the main engine has shut down on a protective trip, the trip is identified before any attempt to restart. The text does not specify a minimum power setting below which the ship would no longer be allowed to continue operating.

answers.question: How often does someone working alone down in the machinery space have to show they are still all right?
answers.expected_fact: reset at intervals not exceeding thirty minutes
answers.answer: According to document [1], a person working alone in an otherwise unattended space must reset the personnel alarm system at intervals not exceeding thirty minutes. Failure to do so raises a pre-alarm, and if still unanswered, a general alarm on the bridge and in the accommodation. This is referred to as the "dead man" alarm.

answers.question: How much oil can be left in the water before we are not allowed to pump it over the side?
answers.expected_fact: 15 parts per million
answers.answer: According to document [1], "Oily mixture from machinery space bilges may be discharged to sea only through approved filtering equipment and only when the oil content of the effluent does not exceed 15 parts per million." This is a ceiling, not a permission.

answers.question: How much oil is put onto the cylinder walls for each unit of power the engine makes?
answers.expected_fact: 0.8 grams per kilowatt hour
answers.answer: According to document [1], the feed rate of cylinder oil is set to 0.8 grams per kilowatt hour at normal service load.

answers.question: If we have to swap the water in the tanks the old way at sea, how far from shore do we need to be?
answers.expected_fact: at least two hundred nautical miles from the nearest land
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, if exchange is used as a contingency measure, it must be carried out at least 200 nautical miles from the nearest land.

answers.question: What does the D-2 standard require?
answers.expected_fact: fewer than ten viable organisms per cubic metre of fifty micrometres or greater
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, the D-2 standard requires that discharged ballast water must contain fewer than ten viable organisms per cubic metre that are fifty micrometres or greater in minimum dimension, and fewer than ten viable organisms per millilitre that are between ten and fifty micrometres.

answers.question: What is the gravity disc selected for?
answers.expected_fact: the density of the fuel in service
answers.answer: The gravity disc is fitted to the fuel oil purifier and is selected for the density of the fuel in service. [1]

answers.question: What is the cascade tank and what is it watched for?
answers.expected_fact: condensate returns there and it is observed for oil contamination
answers.answer:
The cascade tank is mentioned in document index "1" title "Auxiliary Boiler and Steam System". According to this document, the cascade tank accommodates thermal expansion and provides a static head at the pump suction. It is also where condensate returns after being observed for oil contamination.

The text does not explicitly state what the cascade tank is watched for, but it mentions that condensate is observed for oil contamination before being returned to the boiler.

answers.question: What is the critical speed range of the shaft line?
answers.expected_fact: between forty-two and fifty-eight revolutions per minute
answers.answer: The provided documents state that the shaft line has a first-order torsional resonance between forty-two and fifty-eight revolutions per minute.

answers.question: Is it ever permitted to run continuously inside the critical speed range?
answers.expected_fact: No — prohibited under any circumstance
answers.answer: According to the provided documents, sustained operation within the resonance band (critical speed range) is prohibited under any circumstance.

answers.question: Can sludge be discharged to sea if its oil content is below the 15 ppm limit?
answers.expected_fact: No — sludge is not discharged to sea under any circumstance
answers.answer:
According to document [1], oily mixture from machinery space bilges may be discharged to sea only through approved filtering equipment and only when the oil content of the effluent does not exceed 15 parts per million. However, this does not apply to sludge.

Document [2] states that sludge is not discharged to sea under any circumstance.

answers.question: Does the fifty degree exhaust deviation rule apply to the turbocharger inlet temperature?
answers.expected_fact: No — it is not subject to the fifty-degree deviation rule
answers.answer: According to document [1], the fifty-degree deviation rule does not apply to the turbocharger inlet temperature. The text states that "The turbocharger inlet temperature is a separate measurement and is not subject to the fifty-degree deviation rule, because it is a mixed temperature drawn from all cylinders and has no per-cylinder mean to deviate from."

answers.question: Is water washing the turbine side the correct response to turbocharger surge?
answers.expected_fact: No — washing is a routine interval task, not a response to surge
answers.answer: According to document [1], "Turbocharger turbine side water washing is carried out every 250 running hours." Additionally, it states that "Washing a surging machine at load will not clear the condition and may crack the nozzle ring through thermal shock." This implies that water washing of the turbine side is not a response to surge.

answers.question: What is the chloride limit?
answers.expected_fact: ambiguous: jacket cooling water 50 ppm, boiler water 100 ppm
answers.answer:
According to the provided documents, there are two separate chloride limits mentioned:

1. For the closed fresh water circuit, the chloride content must not exceed 50 parts per million.
2. For the auxiliary boiler and steam system, the chloride content of the boiler water must not exceed 100 parts per million.

These limits apply to different systems and are not interchangeable.
